deck_title: Torricelli-Castelli R(z) = R0*(1 + 2gz/v0^2)^(-1/4) free-falling liquid vein gravity contraction vs naive constant-radius cylinder rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Benedetto Castelli (1628) & Evangelista Torricelli (1644) free-falling liquid vein gravity contraction law (combining Torricelli gravity acceleration v(z) = sqrt(v_0^2 + 2*g*z) = v_0*(1 + u) with steady incompressible continuity Q = pi*R(z)^2*v(z) = Q_0 so R(z) = R_0*(1 + 2*g*z/v_0^2)^(-1/4) = R_0 / sqrt(1 + u), locking Q(z)/Q_0 = 1.0000x across all 17 gravity-speed stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive constant-radius cylinder pouring shader (R(z) = R_0, which bloats volumetric flux and cross-section by v(z)/v_0 = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Bernoulli streamtube continuity quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: 3D kitchen faucet water streams, teapot/espresso pouring, molten glass/honey ribbons, chocolate fountains, and waterfall veins
Tapering vertex radius by the exact quarter-power gravity law R(z) = R_0 * (1 + 2*g*z / v_0^2)^(-1/4) so volumetric flow Q(z) = A(z)*v(z) is strictly conserved
Feeding the local tapered radius R(z) into Rayleigh-Plateau pinch-off wavelength lambda^*(z) = 9.015 * R(z)
not_for: Zero-gravity space station liquid extrusion where g = 0
